SRC-334:R003.text: 2. The adapter registry likewise describes the host flow as a reference for native implementation. The selected tests drive that reference controller directly. That is insufficient evidence that the installed ZAICODE host actually dispatches the next model turn. REQUIRED INVESTIGATION: Trace one real invocation: 1. Model turn starts. 2. Model performs tool calls. 3. Canonical state changes. 4. Model emits final response. 5. Native host reports model-turn termination. 6. Canonical iteration verdict is obtained. 7. Host selects the controller action. 8. AUTO_KICK is scheduled durably. 9. Next model turn actually starts. 10. Original Work resumes. Record the first missing boundary. Do not assume it is necessarily SAIPEN code. If the native host cannot implement dispatch from its current adapter API, report the exact missing capability and prepare a separate host-owner integration handoff. Do not pretend a reference controller provides that capability. Do not change the runtime registry to claim stronger enforcement without measuring actual installed behavior. REQUIRED FIX: An operational model turn returning final text must never close the engineering campaign by itself. KICK_NEXT_ITERATION must correspond to an actual admitted dispatch, not simply a returned Python string. Each dispatch requires: - campaign identity - original goal binding - current project lineage - host execution generation - exact scheduled iteration id - original authority proof - idempotency key - checkpoint reference Repeated callbacks must not schedule duplicate turns. A crash after queueing but before dispatch must not lose the work. A crash after dispatch but before acknowledgment must not dispatch a second concurrent generation. A model/provider switch must preserve Work and revalidate capabilities. No new fake operator event may be created. SUCCESS: A real host runs at least five successive operational iterations without another human prompt while Work remains eligible. Every turn is bound to the same authorized objective. SRC-334:R004.text: 3. The current report also treats IDLE, MAX_CYCLES and MAX_WALL as successful stop results. A bounded worker finishing successfully is useful. However, it must not be interpreted as the completion of a durable multi-hour or multi-day campaign. REQUIRED ARCHITECTURE: Keep the current bounded worker. Add the smallest durable orchestration layer that supervises successive worker generations. Do not convert one worker into a single enormous process. The campaign controller owns: CAMPAIGN OBJECTIVE EXECUTION GENERATIONS MAINTENANCE DISCOVERY WAKE CONDITIONS RESOURCE BUDGET STOP POLICY Canonical SAIPEN owns: STATE BOARD LOG SOURCE AUDIT INBOX WORK VERIFICATION AUTHORITY PROOF Do not duplicate those canonical stores. REQUIRED STATES: ADMITTED RUNNING CHECKPOINTING DISCOVERING FORENSIC_ANALYSIS AUDIT_DELIVERY REPAIRING VERIFYING QUIESCENT_WAIT RETRY_WAIT OPERATOR_BLOCKED AUTHORITY_BLOCKED SAFETY_STOP CANCELLED COMPLETE Campaign completion requires an actual terminal contract. A worker reaching MAX_CYCLES is a slice boundary. A worker reaching MAX_WALL is a slice boundary. A worker reporting IDLE requires a complete eligibility assessment before the campaign may enter QUIESCENT_WAIT. Persist the controller objective through process and host restarts. The persistence schema must include: campaign_id project_lineage goal_binding authority_proof_reference authority_scope campaign_state current_work worker_generation last_journal_event last_source_generation last_audit_generation last_saipal_generation last_productive_progress last_verified_result next_action wake_condition retry_count resource_budget created_at updated_at Use an existing canonical storage abstraction where feasible. SRC-334:R005.text: 4. P0 — CREATE AN AUTOMATIC SAIPAL DISCOVERY TRIGGER: PROJECT OWNERSHIP: SAIPEN owns orchestration and authorized ingestion. SAIPAL owns forensic observation and audit qualification. The current SAIPEN snapshot has no discovered production caller that automatically launches SAIPAL after Work exhaustion. Implement a real caller, not a standalone unused helper. SAIPAL commands available in the previously supplied SAIPAL revision include: saipal --json status saipal --json next saipal trigger saipal cpall saipal cpall --status saipal report saipal operator-queue Verify exact installed syntax and supported arguments before using these interfaces. DISCOVERY TRIGGER: Invoke forensic discovery when: - normal authorized Work is exhausted; - relevant recovery is complete; - no higher-priority actionable source exists; - maintenance discovery is authorized; - SAIPAL runtime binding is proven; - analysis source enrollment is valid; - budget is available; - new evidence exists or a periodic check is due. SAIPAL must not be run on a hot loop against unchanged session data. IMPLEMENT: A typed SAIPAL backend adapter inside the SAIPEN campaign controller. Minimum interface: probe() discover() start_or_resume() checkpoint() collect_findings() collect_publication_receipts() get_dispositions() classify_retry() get_next_eligibility() This is a logical interface. Do not introduce new wrappers where existing commands already provide the required contracts. Classify results: ANALYSIS_PROGRESS NEW_QUALIFIED_FINDINGS NO_NEW_EVIDENCE STAGED_PUBLICATION DELIVERED_PUBLICATION SOURCE_NOT_ENROLLED RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE AUTHORITY_REQUIRED ANALYSIS_BLOCKED RETRYABLE_FAILURE PERMANENT_FAILURE No new findings is not an execution error. A source-enrollment problem is not a clean forensic completion. A rejected finding is not a reason to repeat its analysis immediately. SAIPAL may not modify SAIPEN implementation files. SRC-334:R008.text: 7. P1 — BREAK THE NO-PROGRESS / FALSE-VICTORY CYCLE: Separate: MODEL_TURN_FINISHED WORK_ITEM_FINISHED SLICE_FINISHED MAINTENANCE_PASS_FINISHED FORENSIC_PASS_FINISHED QUEUE_DRAINED CAMPAIGN_QUIESCENT CAMPAIGN_COMPLETE These are different events. Never substitute one for another. A new model response does not constitute progress. A fresh checkpoint timestamp does not constitute progress. A repeated test PASS over identical evidence does not constitute new engineering progress. Useful progress includes: - newly verified implementation change - real lifecycle advancement - confirmed recovery - new source generation - newly accepted audit - newly reproduced defect - new verified closure - resolved authoritative blocker Record a semantic fingerprint over relevant stable inputs. Do not include volatile timestamps or model-generated wording in the progress identity. If the same objective repeats with unchanged evidence: - stop immediate redispatch; - record the unchanged fingerprint; - calculate a bounded retry or eligibility condition; - enter QUIESCENT_WAIT or a typed blocker state; - resume when evidence or authority genuinely changes. Preserve existing NO_PROGRESS_LOOP and watchdog protections. Do not remove an anti-loop guard to make a 24-hour run superficially stay active. A quiet controller is preferable to a costly meaningless loop.

The full route must be demonstrated: OPERATOR AUTHORIZATION ↓ CAMPAIGN ADMISSION ↓ REAL WORK EXECUTION ↓ MODEL TURN FINISHES ↓ NATIVE HOST SCHEDULES NEXT TURN ↓ WORK COMPLETES ↓ BOARD EXHAUSTION ↓ MAINTENANCE ELIGIBILITY ↓ SAIPAL DISCOVERY ↓ QUALIFIED FORENSIC AUDIT ↓ AUTHORIZED PUBLICATION ↓ SAIPEN AUDIT INGESTION ↓ CANONICAL REPAIR WORK ↓ REGRESSION VERIFICATION ↓ MAINTAINER DISPOSITION ↓ SAIPAL CLOSED LOOP ↓ NEXT ELIGIBILITY ASSESSMENT Demonstrate every arrow with actual source and runtime evidence. A diagram or mock of this route is not sufficient acceptance. Run: 1. Focused unit regressions. 2. Source/production caller tests. 3. Crash and concurrency tests. 4. Installed-host parity tests. 5. Real host scheduling tests. 6. SAIPAL bridge tests. 7. Real audit-to-repair closed-loop test. 8. Multi-generation controller test. 9. Extended unattended soak. 10. Final conformance/release gating. For the extended soak, prefer several hours of actual execution with real worker turnover and quiet intervals. If the required host or access is unavailable, report the precise missing integration and do not claim soak completion. A simulated 24-hour clock does not prove 24-hour runtime reliability. A multi-hour process that only wakes and prints status does not prove multi-hour productive engineering. Measure: elapsed time productive time quiescent time worker generations successful recoveries new qualified findings new accepted Work verified fixes failed verification attempts duplicate suppression operator handbacks unauthorized mutations token consumption provider failures Acceptance requires zero unauthorized mutations and zero duplicate concurrent campaign owners. SRC-334:R014.text: 13. HONEST COMPLETION CONTRACT: The following do NOT count as completion: - A new maintenance module with no production caller. - A green unit test against a mock host. - A correctly formatted protocol document. - An emitted AUTO_KICK with no native dispatch. - A SAIPAL process that starts but analyzes no eligible evidence. - A staged audit that was never legally delivered. - A delivered audit with no ingestion receipt. - A repair ticket with no reproduction. - A passing test that does not exercise the repaired caller. - A model that announces victory after a single Work item. - A controller that survives for hours by repeating unchanged text. The campaign is successful only when the production system has demonstrated authorized, restartable, self-replenishing execution. If external owner integration is required, preserve the project boundary and create an independently actionable owner-specific handoff. Do not edit unrelated repositories to make the test appear green.

SRC-334:R015.text: 14. REQUIRED FINAL REPORT: STATUS: IMPLEMENTED / PARTIAL / BLOCKED / VERIFIED CAMPAIGN: stable identity and authority scope IMPLEMENTED: exact changed paths and symbols PRODUCTION CALLERS: exact invocation chains FALSE-IDLE: original reproduction and fixed behavior HOST AUTO-KICK: real native dispatch evidence SAIPAL BRIDGE: read / stage / publish / ingest status AUDIT-TO-REPAIR: exact linked finding, receipt, ticket and disposition DURABILITY: lease and restart evidence TESTS: counts, commands, results, exclusions LIVE SOAK: actual runtime duration and execution generations SAFETY: authority and negative-control results REMAINING DEFECTS: reproducible evidence only BLOCKERS: owner, scope, source and exact release condition NEXT EXACT ACTION: executable canonical action or genuine stop reason FINAL DIRECTIVE The objective is not to keep a single model response alive. The objective is to keep an authorized engineering campaign alive across many model responses, independent worker generations and temporary runtime interruptions. Do not confuse a completed slice with a completed objective. Do not confuse a green local test with a connected production route. Do not confuse the absence of currently runnable Work with the exhaustion of every eligible discovery source. Implement the real mechanism, verify it end-to-end and continue until a legitimate campaign boundary is reached. ====================================================================== END SAIHANDOFF ======================================================================
